transcript: This week alone, I have audited around five fashion, jewellery and accessory brands on meta spending anywhere between $50,000 per month up to about $300,000 per month. And the, I guess the mistakes or the troubleshooting that I'm finding is quite similar between these accounts and I thought I would share them with you. So No. 1 is there's this big push for creative volume, which I am all about, but there needs to be some streamline into how we're dumping creative into the account. Right now, I feel for a lot of brands, it's just like, let's just do all this creative and shove it into an ad set and see what happens. And there's actually no system behind it. There's no reasoning for should this be a new ad set? Cause essentially it's a new angle or this is a new positioning of the brand and should we actually be testing it separate aside the other creatives that we are doing? For example, we had one brand putting their gifting, um, creatives for their specific product in with their everyday creatives and that just confuses the algorithm of to who to go after. I think everyone's talking about creative diversification, but I just still am not seeing enough of it. It's just campaign content for a lot of these high end brands within the ad account, which that does serve a place. But as you know, I've mentioned this a million times, it's only a small part of Your brand strategy, there is only so much meta will identify that as a new ad. So you need to be thinking about how can you fulfill your pillars. So whether this is content from U G, C creators, is it customer content, is it creating gifts? Is it creating unboxing videos showing the pieces on like clothes rack? How can you create different styles of content that isn't just your campaign shoot? And No. 3, it's actually not specifically ad related, but it's post click, which is really important to discuss. We do a lot of testing with fashion brands and jewellery brands and all our brands that we work with actually on where is the right directional, um, destination to send people after a click. And believe it or not, this actually varies per client and her kind of niche. So there's not a one size fits all approach. But a lot of the things that I was seeing is either sending them to like the homepage, which isn't the right thing at all for a fashion brand or sending them potentially to a collection page with a product page could have a higher conversion rate or sometimes sending them to a product page where the collection page could have a better yielding conversion rate. So really dissecting where the ads are going post click to help improve, um, the ad results. So these are the big mistakes.
